claims.evidence: NHS offers at least two scans (11-14 weeks and 18-21 weeks); combined test and Down's/Edwards'/Patau's screening are optional; booking-stage blood tests described by trusts.
Booking appointment usually 8 to 12 weeks; midwife checks blood pressure and urine; blood tests described at booking by trusts.
Retrieved: dating scan at 11 to 14 weeks estimates due date from baby's measurements. 'Development' and 'more than one baby' not seen in retrieved text.
claims.newSentence: The dating scan, usually at 11 to 14 weeks, estimates the due date from the baby's measurements.

claims.evidence: Dating and anomaly scans are offered but you do not have to have them; combined test only 'if you choose'.
Anomaly scan usually 18 to 21 weeks and checks for 11 physical conditions; 'in-depth check of anatomy' wording not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: The mid-pregnancy anomaly scan usually takes place between 18 and 21 weeks and checks for 11 physical conditions in the baby.

claims.evidence: First midwife appointment, called the booking appointment, usually between 8 and 12 weeks.
Retrieved: midwife checks blood pressure and urine and offers a blood group test. Purpose (pre-eclampsia, infection) not in retrieved text.
claims.newSentence: The midwife checks blood pressure and urine and offers a blood group test.

claims.evidence: Trust pages say booking-stage blood tests (infections, haemoglobin conditions) happen early, around 10 weeks or before. Weak: summary blended trust pages.
Retrieved: HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B, sickle cell and thalassaemia tests; arrangements vary by trust and testing is optional. Iron, blood sugar and rubella not seen.
claims.newSentence: NHS trusts describe booking-stage blood tests for HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B, sickle cell and thalassaemia, and the exact list can vary between trusts.

claims.evidence: At least two scans offered, at 11 to 14 weeks and between 18 and 21 weeks.
Retrieved: dating scan estimates due date from measurements and can include the nuchal translucency measurement. 'More than one baby' not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: It estimates when the baby is due from the baby's measurements.

claims.evidence: Fragment answering a question heading (presumably whether screening is required); screening is a choice. Check the heading reads 'Is it compulsory?' or similar.
Combined screening only 'if you choose to have this screening'; scans offered but optional.
Combined test is a blood test at 10 to 14 weeks plus a nuchal translucency scan measuring fluid at the back of the baby's neck.
The 20-week anomaly scan also screens for Edwards' and Patau's syndromes.
Quadruple test is a blood test at 14 to 20 weeks for Down's syndrome, offered when too late for the combined test or NT cannot be measured.
Quadruple test is not as accurate as the combined test.
Retrieved: second scan, 18 to 21 weeks, checks for 11 physical conditions and placenta position; not every condition can be identified. 'In-depth' not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: The anomaly scan is an ultrasound that checks for 11 physical conditions in the baby and the position of the placenta, though not every condition can be found.

claims.evidence: NHS: 18 to 21 weeks; one trust says 20 to 22 weeks.
The 20-week anomaly scan also screens for Edwards' and Patau's syndromes.
A higher-chance result does not mean the baby definitely has the condition; screening is not diagnostic.
After a higher-chance result you can choose between one further NIPT, a diagnostic test (CVS or amniocentesis) or no further testing.
NHS states there are no known risks to you or your baby from the blood tests or scans.
Retrieved: diagnostic tests (CVS, amniocentesis) give a definite answer, unlike screening. 'Discussed with midwife or specialist beforehand' not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: Diagnostic tests, such as chorionic villus sampling or amniocentesis, are different from screening and can give a definite answer.

claims.evidence: Higher-chance results are phoned or given in person within about a week; lower-chance results come by letter, usually within 2 weeks.
Generic signposting; the clinical examples (bleeding, reduced movements) were not retrieved so are removed.
claims.newSentence: For urgent concerns in pregnancy, the midwife, maternity unit or NHS 111 can advise, and 999 is for emergencies.
